reason: The passage explicitly demonstrates Yahweh's care for His people through multiple textual markers: (1) God perceives the suffering of the Israelites - 'And now behold, the cry of the children of Israel has come to me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them' (וְעַתָּה הִנֵּה צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלַי וְגַם־ רָאִיתִי אֶת־ הַלַּחַץ); (2) God actively responds to this suffering by commissioning Moses to liberate them - 'And now come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, and bring out my people, the children of Israel, from Egypt' (וְעַתָּה לְכָה וְאֶשְׁלָחֲךָ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה וְהוֹצֵא אֶת־ עַמִּי); (3) God establishes personal continuity with the patriarchs, identifying Himself as 'the God of your fathers.' The pattern of divine attentiveness to suffering and intervention for deliverance is the hallmark of covenantal care in the Hebrew Bible.
